question:
Consider the following statements about Golconda Fort:

1. It served as the capital of the Qutb Shahi dynasty.

2. It is renowned for an acoustic system by which a clap at the Fateh Darwaza can be heard at the hilltop pavilion.

3. The Kohinoor diamond is believed to have once been stored in its vaults.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1, 2 and 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• All three statements are correct. Golconda Fort stands on a granite hill near Hyderabad, Telangana. (गोलकुंडा किला — तेलंगाना)

 

• Statement 1 is correct: Originally a mud fort of the Kakatiyas, it was rebuilt in granite and served as the capital of the Qutb Shahi dynasty from 1518 until the capital was shifted to Hyderabad in 1590. It fell to Aurangzeb in 1687.

 

• Statement 2 is correct: The fort is famous for its remarkable acoustics. A hand-clap at the Fateh Darwaza, the main entrance, can be heard clearly at the Bala Hisar pavilion at the hilltop, nearly a kilometre away — a device that served as an early-warning system.

 

• Statement 3 is correct: The Golconda mines in the region were once the world's principal source of diamonds, and the Kohinoor, along with the Hope and the Darya-i-Noor, is believed to have been stored in the fort's vaults.

 

• The fort also has a sophisticated system of water supply using Persian wheels, and its outer wall runs for about 10 km with 87 semi-circular bastions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other well-known Indian forts:

◦ Gwalior Fort, Madhya Pradesh — called the "pearl among fortresses" by Babur; its southern face has rock-cut Jain Tirthankara images, and the Teli ka Mandir and Sas-Bahu temples stand within it

◦ Red Fort, Delhi — built by Shah Jahan; a UNESCO World Heritage Site

◦ Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore, Amber, Jaisalmer and Gagron — the six Hill Forts of Rajasthan, a UNESCO World Heritage Site (2013)

◦ Daulatabad (Devagiri) Fort, Maharashtra — to which Muhammad bin Tughlaq shifted his capital

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 are incorrect because each of them omits at least one statement that is factually accurate.

question: Which Sufi order (silsila) was established in India by Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Chishti order.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Chishti silsila was established in India by Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti, who came to India around 1192 and settled at Ajmer, where his tomb, the Ajmer Sharif Dargah, remains one of the most visited shrines in the country. (ख़्वाजा मुईनुद्दीन चिश्ती — चिश्ती सिलसिला)

 

• The Chishtis were the most popular Sufi order in India. They emphasised simplicity, poverty, service to humanity, tolerance towards all faiths, and refused to accept state patronage or government office. They made extensive use of sama (devotional music).

 

• Prominent Chishti saints include Qutbuddin Bakhtiyar Kaki (Delhi), Baba Fariduddin Ganj-i-Shakar (Punjab), whose verses are included in the Guru Granth Sahib, Nizamuddin Auliya (Delhi), and Nasiruddin Chiragh-i-Delhi.

 

• Sufi terminology worth remembering: khanqah (hospice), pir or murshid (spiritual guide), murid (disciple), silsila (order or chain of succession), sama (musical assembly) and urs (death anniversary of a saint).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Bhakti movement distinguished two broad forms of worship: Saguna, devotion to God with attributes and form, as in the worship of Rama or Krishna by Tulsidas, Surdas and Mirabai; and Nirguna, devotion to a formless, attribute-less God, as with Kabir, Guru Nanak and Dadu Dayal.

 

• The Bhakti movement began in South India between the seventh and ninth centuries with the Alvars (devotees of Vishnu) and the Nayanars (devotees of Shiva).

 

NOTE

 

• The Suhrawardi order (Option 2): Established in India by Bahauddin Zakariya at Multan; unlike the Chishtis, its saints accepted state patronage and official posts.

 

• The Qadiriyya order (Option 3): Founded by Shaikh Abdul Qadir Jilani and popular in Punjab and Sindh; Dara Shikoh was associated with it.

 

• The Naqshbandi order (Option 4): Introduced in India by Khwaja Baqi Billah; its best-known figure was Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi, who opposed the liberal policies of Akbar.

question: Which of the following best describes the contribution of Sant Kabir to the Bhakti movement?
option_1: He composed the Ramcharitmanas in the Awadhi dialect
option_2: He founded the Varkari tradition centred on the deity Vithoba at Pandharpur
option_3: He composed dohas in a mixed vernacular speech, rejecting ritualism and caste distinctions, and many of his verses were included in the Guru Granth Sahib
option_4: He wrote devotional kirtans exclusively in Sanskrit for use in temple ritual
solution_text:
The correct answer is He composed dohas in a mixed vernacular speech, rejecting ritualism and caste distinctions, and many of his verses were included in the Guru Granth Sahib.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sant Kabir (15th century) was the foremost saint of the Nirguna stream of the Bhakti movement, which worships a formless God without attributes. (संत कबीर — निर्गुण भक्ति धारा)

 

• He composed dohas (couplets), sakhis and pads in a mixed popular speech often called Sadhukkadi — a blend of Awadhi, Braj and Bhojpuri — so that ordinary people, not scholars, could understand him.

 

• He attacked ritualism, idol worship, pilgrimage, fasting, the caste system and the claims of both Brahmanical priests and the ulema, and preached the unity of God, whom he called by names drawn from both traditions.

 

• A large number of his verses were incorporated into the Guru Granth Sahib, compiled by Guru Arjan Dev. His compositions are also collected in the Bijak, Kabir Granthavali and Anurag Sagar. He is said to have been a disciple of Ramananda, and his followers are known as Kabirpanthis.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major Bhakti saints and their contributions:

◦ Tulsidas — the Ramcharitmanas in Awadhi

◦ Surdas — the Sursagar, in Braj, on the childhood of Krishna

◦ Mirabai — Rajasthani and Gujarati padas devoted to Krishna

◦ Guru Nanak — founder of Sikhism, a Nirguna saint

◦ Chaitanya Mahaprabhu — Krishna bhakti and sankirtan in Bengal

◦ Annamacharya — the earliest known Telugu composer of sankirtanas, who wrote about 32,000 songs in praise of Lord Venkateswara, promoting devotion and social equality

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: The Ramcharitmanas was composed by Tulsidas.

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: The Varkari tradition of Maharashtra, centred on Vithoba at Pandharpur, is associated with Jnaneshwar, Namdev, Eknath and Tukaram.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: Kabir deliberately avoided Sanskrit and the temple ritual he criticised, composing instead in the language of the common people.

question: Why is the surface of a golf ball covered with dimples?
option_1: The dimples make the ball heavier so that it rolls more steadily on the green
option_2: The dimples are required by the rules so that the manufacturer can be identified
option_3: The dimples reduce aerodynamic drag and help generate lift, so that the ball travels considerably farther
option_4: The dimples help the ball grip the club face and prevent it from spinning
solution_text:
The correct answer is The dimples reduce aerodynamic drag and help generate lift, so that the ball travels considerably farther.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The dimples on a golf ball create a thin layer of turbulent air clinging to the surface of the ball. This turbulent boundary layer stays attached to the ball for longer, so the low-pressure wake behind the ball is narrower and the pressure drag is roughly halved. (गोल्फ बॉल के डिंपल — वायुगतिकीय ड्रैग में कमी)

 

• The dimples also interact with the backspin imparted by the club to generate lift through the Magnus effect, which keeps the ball airborne longer.

 

• The combined effect is dramatic: a dimpled ball travels roughly twice as far as a perfectly smooth ball struck with the same force. A modern golf ball typically carries between 300 and 500 dimples.

 

• The maximum permitted weight of a golf ball is about 45.93 grams and its minimum diameter about 42.67 mm, under the rules of the R&A and the USGA.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Common golf terms: birdie (one stroke under par), eagle (two under), albatross (three under), bogey (one over), par, tee, caddie, putt, fairway, bunker and hole in one.

 

• The four Major championships in men's golf are the Masters, the PGA Championship, the US Open and the Open Championship. Anirban Lahiri, Jeev Milkha Singh, Shubhankar Sharma and Aditi Ashok are leading Indian golfers.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: Dimples do not add weight; the weight of a golf ball is fixed by the rules.

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: Manufacturers are identified by markings printed on the ball, not by the dimple pattern.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: Backspin is imparted by the grooves on the club face, and spin is in fact essential to a golf shot, not something to be prevented.

question: The Permanent Settlement of Bengal, introduced in 1793, is associated with which Governor-General?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lord Cornwallis.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Permanent Settlement, also called the Zamindari system or the Istamrari Bandobast, was introduced in 1793 by Lord Cornwallis in Bengal, Bihar and Odisha, and later extended to parts of the Northern Circars and Varanasi. (स्थायी बंदोबस्त, 1793 — लॉर्ड कॉर्नवालिस)

 

• Under it the zamindars were recognised as the owners of the land and made responsible for collecting and paying a fixed land revenue permanently, which was never to be raised. The zamindar had to pay by sunset of the appointed day, failing which his estate would be auctioned — the Sunset Law.

 

• The state's share was fixed at 10/11ths of the rental, leaving the zamindar one-eleventh. The system gave the Company a stable and predictable income and created a class of loyal landlords, but it impoverished the actual cultivators, who had no security of tenure.

 

• Cornwallis is also remembered for the Cornwallis Code (1793), the separation of revenue and judicial functions, and the reorganisation of the civil service on the basis of merit and adequate salaries — for which he is called the "Father of the Indian Civil Service".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The other two major British land revenue systems:

◦ Ryotwari system — introduced by Thomas Munro and Alexander Read in Madras and later Bombay; settlement made directly with the cultivator (ryot), revised periodically

◦ Mahalwari system — introduced by Holt Mackenzie and later revised by William Bentinck in the North Western Provinces, Punjab and parts of central India; settlement made with the village or mahal as a whole

 

• Warren Hastings was the first Governor-General of Bengal (1773), Lord Wellesley introduced the Subsidiary Alliance, and Lord William Bentinck became the first Governor-General of India in 1833 and abolished sati in 1829.

 

NOTE

 

• Warren Hastings (Option 1): Introduced the short-lived system of farming out revenue by auction and the Diwani Adalats and Faujdari Adalats.

 

• Lord Wellesley (Option 3): Known for the Subsidiary Alliance and the founding of Fort William College.

 

• Lord William Bentinck (Option 4): Known for social reforms — the abolition of sati and the suppression of thuggee — and for making English the medium of higher education.

question:
Fill in the blanks:

At the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics, P.T. Usha finished fourth in the women's 400 metres hurdles, missing the bronze medal by ______ of a second.
solution_text:
The correct answer is one-hundredth.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the 1984 Los Angeles Olympics, P.T. Usha finished fourth in the women's 400 metres hurdles, missing the bronze medal by just one-hundredth (1/100th) of a second. (पी. टी. उषा — 1984 लॉस एंजिल्स ओलंपिक)

 

• Her time of 55.42 seconds remained the Indian national record for many years. She thereby became the first Indian woman to reach the final of an Olympic track event.

 

• Known as the "Payyoli Express" and the "Golden Girl of India", she was born at Payyoli in Kerala and trained under coach O.M. Nambiar.

 

• She won a large haul of medals at the Asian Games and the Asian Athletics Championships, and was awarded the Arjuna Award (1984) and the Padma Shri (1985). She was elected President of the Indian Olympic Association in 2022, becoming the first sportswoman to hold the post, and has served as a nominated Member of the Rajya Sabha.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Milkha Singh, the "Flying Sikh", finished fourth in the men's 400 metres at the 1960 Rome Olympics with a timing of 45.6 seconds, a national record that stood until 1984 — a near-miss often paired with P.T. Usha's in examinations.

 

• India's Olympic athletics medal came only in 2020 (Tokyo), when Neeraj Chopra won gold in the javelin throw; he followed it with a silver at Paris 2024.

 

NOTE

 

• One-tenth (Option 1), one-thousandth (Option 2) and half (Option 3) are incorrect. The margin is famously recorded as 1/100th of a second, one of the narrowest fourth-place finishes in Olympic history.

question:
Which of the following statements correctly reflect the Goods and Services Tax (GST) regime in India?

1) GST was introduced with effect from 1 July 2017 through the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act.

2) Petroleum crude, high-speed diesel, petrol, natural gas and aviation turbine fuel have been kept outside the levy of GST for the time being.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 and 2 Both are correct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct. The Goods and Services Tax came into force on 1 July 2017, given effect by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016, which inserted Article 246A, Article 269A and Article 279A into the Constitution. (जीएसटी — 1 जुलाई 2017, 101वां संविधान संशोधन)

 

• Statement 2 is correct. Five petroleum products — crude petroleum, high-speed diesel, petrol (motor spirit), natural gas and aviation turbine fuel — have been kept outside GST for the time being, and continue to attract central excise duty and state VAT. The GST Council may bring them under GST at a future date. Alcoholic liquor for human consumption is permanently excluded by the Constitution.

 

• GST is a destination-based, multi-stage, comprehensive indirect tax levied on the supply of goods and services, with credit available for tax paid at earlier stages, so that the tax falls only on value addition.

 

• Its components are CGST (levied by the Centre), SGST/UTGST (by States and Union Territories) on intra-State supplies, and IGST (by the Centre) on inter-State supplies and imports.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The GST Council (Article 279A) is chaired by the Union Finance Minister, with the Union Minister of State for Finance and the finance ministers of all States as members. Decisions require a three-fourths majority of weighted votes, the Centre holding one-third of the total votes and the States together two-thirds.

 

• The idea of GST in India was first recommended by the Kelkar Task Force in 2003. The concept of a value-added tax originated in France, which adopted it in 1954.

 

• Assam was the first state to ratify the GST Constitutional Amendment Bill.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are incorrect because both of the given statements are factually accurate.

question: The Salt Lake Stadium, officially known as the Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan and one of the largest football stadiums in India, is located in which city?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kolkata.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Salt Lake Stadium, officially the Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan (VYBK), is located at Bidhannagar (Salt Lake City) in Kolkata, West Bengal. (साल्ट लेक स्टेडियम — कोलकाता)

 

• Opened in 1984, it is the largest football stadium in India by capacity and was among the largest in the world before its capacity was reduced during renovation. It hosted the final of the FIFA U-17 World Cup in 2017.

 

• It is the home ground of the Kolkata clubs East Bengal, Mohun Bagan and Mohammedan Sporting, and hosts the Kolkata Derby.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Some important Indian stadiums and their locations:

◦ Narendra Modi Stadium, Motera, Ahmedabad — the world's largest cricket stadium

◦ Eden Gardens, Kolkata — India's oldest cricket ground, established 1864

◦ Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium and Arun Jaitley (Feroz Shah Kotla) Stadium — New Delhi

◦ Major Dhyan Chand National Stadium, New Delhi — hockey

◦ Kalinga Stadium, Bhubaneswar — hockey; hosted the Hockey World Cup

◦ Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai — venue of the 2011 Cricket World Cup final

◦ Chinnaswamy Stadium, Bengaluru and Chepauk (M.A. Chidambaram) Stadium, Chennai

◦ Dr. Shyama Prasad Mookerjee Swimming Pool Complex — New Delhi

 

NOTE

 

• Guwahati (Option 2): Has the Indira Gandhi Athletic Stadium and the Barsapara Cricket Stadium.

 

• Bhubaneswar (Option 3): Has the Kalinga Stadium, a major hockey venue.

 

• Patna (Option 4): Has the Moin-ul-Haq Stadium.

question: Which of the following statements accurately describes 'A Suitable Boy' by Vikram Seth?
option_1: One of the longest novels written in English, set in post-Independence India, which won the Commonwealth Writers' Prize for Best Book
option_2: It is a memoir of the author's career as a cardiologist in the United States
option_3: It won the Booker Prize in 1993 for its portrayal of the Partition
option_4: It is a Hindi novel later translated into English by the author himself
solution_text:
The correct answer is One of the longest novels written in English, set in post-Independence India, which won the Commonwealth Writers' Prize for Best Book.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'A Suitable Boy' (1993) by Vikram Seth is among the longest novels ever published in a single volume in English, running to about 1,350 pages and roughly 591,000 words. (ए सूटेबल बॉय — विक्रम सेठ)

 

• It is set in the early 1950s in a newly independent India, and follows Mrs. Rupa Mehra's search for a suitable husband for her daughter Lata, against the background of the first general election, land reform and communal tension.

 

• It won the Commonwealth Writers' Prize for Best Book and the WH Smith Literary Award. A sequel, 'A Suitable Girl', has long been announced.

 

• Vikram Seth's other well-known works include 'The Golden Gate', a novel written entirely in sonnets, 'An Equal Music', 'Two Lives' and the travelogue 'From Heaven Lake', which won the Thomas Cook Travel Book Award.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Indian-origin winners of the Booker Prize: V.S. Naipaul (1971), Salman Rushdie (1981, *Midnight's Children*), Arundhati Roy (1997, *The God of Small Things*), Kiran Desai (2006, *The Inheritance of Loss*) and Aravind Adiga (2008, *The White Tiger*).

 

• 'Heart: A History' is a non-fiction work by the cardiologist Sandeep Jauhar tracing the history of the human heart and of cardiac medicine; being non-fiction, it falls outside the scope of the Edgar Award for Best Novel, which is given for crime fiction by the Mystery Writers of America.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: That description fits the medical memoirs of Sandeep Jauhar, not Vikram Seth.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: 'A Suitable Boy' was not awarded the Booker Prize; the 1993 Booker went to Roddy Doyle for *Paddy Clarke Ha Ha Ha*.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: The novel was written originally in English.

question: An oxbow lake is formed by which of the following processes?
option_1: The cutting off of a meander loop of a river from its main channel
option_2: The damming of a valley by a glacial moraine
option_3: The collapse of the roof of a limestone cavern
option_4: The deposition of sand by wind in a desert basin
solution_text:
The correct answer is The cutting off of a meander loop of a river from its main channel.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• An oxbow lake is a crescent-shaped lake formed when a meander loop of a river is cut off from the main channel. (गोखुर झील — नदी विसर्प का कटकर अलग होना)

 

• The process works like this: in its middle and lower course a river swings from side to side, eroding the outer, concave bank where the current is fastest and depositing on the inner, convex bank. The neck of the loop grows progressively narrower until, usually during a flood, the river cuts across the neck and takes the shorter course. The abandoned loop is sealed off by deposition and survives as an oxbow lake.

 

• Oxbow lakes are typical of floodplains; in India they are common along the Ganga and the Brahmaputra. In Australia such lakes are called billabongs.

 

• Other landforms of river deposition include floodplains, natural levees, point bars, alluvial fans, deltas and meanders; landforms of river erosion include V-shaped valleys, gorges, canyons, waterfalls, potholes and river terraces.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• A gorge is a deep valley with very steep, almost vertical sides, formed where a river cuts downward through hard, resistant rock in a region of rapid uplift; a canyon is a gorge in horizontal sedimentary strata, of which the Grand Canyon on the Colorado river is the classic example.

 

• A delta forms where a river's load is deposited as it enters a sea or lake; the Sundarbans delta of the Ganga-Brahmaputra is the largest in the world. The Narmada and Tapi, flowing through rift valleys, form estuaries instead.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: A valley dammed by a moraine forms a glacial or moraine-dammed lake, such as many lakes of the Himalayas.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: The collapse of a cavern roof in limestone produces a sinkhole, doline or karst window.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: Wind deposition in a desert basin produces sand dunes and, where water collects seasonally, playa lakes.

question: Covaxin, India's first indigenously developed COVID-19 vaccine, was developed by Bharat Biotech in collaboration with which institution?
option_1: The CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology, Hyderabad
option_2: The All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi
option_3: The Indian Council of Medical Research and the National Institute of Virology, Pune
option_4: The Serum Institute of India, Pune
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Indian Council of Medical Research and the National Institute of Virology, Pune.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Covaxin (BBV152) was developed by Bharat Biotech International Limited, Hyderabad, in collaboration with the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) and its National Institute of Virology (NIV), Pune, which isolated the virus strain used to make it. (कोवैक्सिन — भारत बायोटेक एवं आईसीएमआर-एनआईवी)

 

• It is a whole-virion inactivated vaccine — the virus is killed so that it cannot cause disease but can still provoke an immune response. It was India's first fully indigenous COVID-19 vaccine and received WHO Emergency Use Listing in November 2021.

 

• India's nationwide vaccination drive began on 16 January 2021, initially with Covaxin and Covishield, the latter being the Oxford-AstraZeneca vaccine manufactured under licence by the Serum Institute of India, Pune.

 

• Other Indian vaccines include ZyCoV-D by Zydus Cadila, the world's first approved DNA vaccine, and Corbevax by Biological E.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), established in 1911 as the Indian Research Fund Association and renamed in 1949, is India's apex body for the formulation and promotion of biomedical research, functioning under the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. Its headquarters are at New Delhi.

 

• The disease COVID-19 is caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus; the World Health Organization declared it a pandemic on 11 March 2020.

 

• The Serum Institute of India is the world's largest vaccine manufacturer by number of doses produced.

 

NOTE

 

• The CSIR-CCMB, Hyderabad (Option 1): Contributed to genome sequencing and surveillance of SARS-CoV-2 variants, but did not co-develop Covaxin.

 

• AIIMS, New Delhi (Option 2): Was one of the clinical trial sites, not a co-developer.

 

• The Serum Institute of India (Option 4): Manufactured Covishield under licence from Oxford-AstraZeneca.

question: According to Census 2011, which state recorded the highest decadal population growth rate during 2001-2011?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Meghalaya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to Census 2011, Meghalaya recorded the highest decadal population growth rate among the states, at about 27.9 per cent for 2001-2011. (मेघालय — सर्वाधिक दशकीय वृद्धि दर)

 

• Nagaland was the only state to record a negative decadal growth rate (about -0.6 per cent) in the same period. Kerala recorded the lowest positive growth among the states, at about 4.9 per cent.

 

• India's overall decadal growth for 2001-2011 was 17.7 per cent, the first decade since Independence in which the absolute increase in population was smaller than in the preceding decade.

 

• Among Union Territories, Dadra and Nagar Haveli recorded the highest decadal growth, at about 55.9 per cent, largely on account of in-migration for industrial work; Lakshadweep recorded the lowest.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other key Census 2011 figures: total population 121.09 crore; sex ratio 943; child sex ratio 919; literacy 74.04 per cent; density 382 persons per sq km; urban population 31.16 per cent.

 

• Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state and Sikkim the least; Rajasthan is the largest state by area and Goa the smallest; Bihar is the most densely populated state and Arunachal Pradesh the least.

 

• The Census is conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner under the Ministry of Home Affairs. The census motto for 2011 was "Our Census, Our Future".

 

NOTE

 

• Bihar (Option 1): Recorded a high growth rate of about 25.4 per cent, the highest among the larger states, but below Meghalaya's.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 3): Grew by about 20.2 per cent and remains the most populous state, but this was not the highest rate.

 

• Jharkhand (Option 4): Grew by about 22.4 per cent.

question: Which of the following best describes the Infant Mortality Rate (IMR)?
option_1: The number of deaths of children below five years of age per 1,000 population
option_2: The number of stillbirths per 1,000 deliveries in a given year
option_3: The number of maternal deaths per 100,000 live births in a given year
option_4: The number of deaths of children below one year of age per 1,000 live births in a given year
solution_text:
The correct answer is The number of deaths of children below one year of age per 1,000 live births in a given year.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) is the number of deaths of infants under one year of age per 1,000 live births in a given year. (शिशु मृत्यु दर — प्रति 1,000 जीवित जन्म)

 

• IMR is regarded as one of the most sensitive indicators of the health status and standard of living of a population, because infant survival depends on maternal health, nutrition, sanitation, safe drinking water and access to medical care.

 

• Important related demographic measures:

◦ Crude Birth Rate (CBR) — live births per 1,000 population in a year

◦ Crude Death Rate (CDR) — deaths per 1,000 population in a year

◦ Rate of Natural Increase — the difference between the birth rate and the death rate, excluding migration

◦ Under-Five Mortality Rate (U5MR) — deaths of children under five per 1,000 live births

◦ Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR) — maternal deaths per 1,00,000 live births

◦ Total Fertility Rate (TFR) — average number of children a woman bears in her lifetime; the replacement level is 2.1

 

• In India IMR has fallen steadily and, as per the Sample Registration System, now stands at about 26 per 1,000 live births. Kerala has consistently recorded the lowest IMR among the states.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Data on births and deaths in India come from the Sample Registration System (SRS), run by the Registrar General of India, and from the National Family Health Survey (NFHS).

 

• Health schemes aimed at reducing infant and maternal mortality include the Janani Suraksha Yojana, Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram, Mission Indradhanush for immunisation, and POSHAN Abhiyaan for nutrition.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: That describes the Under-Five Mortality Rate, and it too is measured per 1,000 live births, not per 1,000 population.

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: That is the stillbirth rate, a separate measure.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: That is the Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR).

question:
Examine the following statements about ISRO's Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV) and select the correct option:

Statement 1: It is designed to place satellites weighing up to about 500 kg into Low Earth Orbit.

Statement 2: It is a four-stage vehicle in which every stage is powered by liquid propulsion.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only Statement 1 is correct.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct. The Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV) is designed to place satellites of up to about 500 kg into a 500 km planar Low Earth Orbit, or about 300 kg into a sun-synchronous orbit. (एसएसएलवी — 500 किग्रा तक का पेलोड)

 

• Statement 2 is incorrect. The SSLV is a three-stage vehicle, and all three stages are solid-propellant stages. Final orbital injection is performed by a liquid-propulsion Velocity Trimming Module (VTM) in the terminal stage. It is therefore neither four-staged nor wholly liquid-propelled.

 

• The SSLV was developed to meet the growing demand for on-demand launch of small satellites. Its advantages are low cost, minimal launch infrastructure, a very short turnaround time, and the ability to accommodate multiple satellites with a small launch team.

 

• SSLV-D2, flown in February 2023, successfully placed EOS-07, Janus-1 and AzaadiSAT-2 into a 450 km circular orbit. SSLV-D3 in August 2024 placed EOS-08 in orbit, completing the vehicle's development flights.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• ISRO's operational launch vehicles:

◦ PSLV — the "workhorse", a four-stage vehicle with alternating solid and liquid stages, used for polar sun-synchronous orbits

◦ GSLV Mk II — for communication satellites in geosynchronous transfer orbit

◦ LVM3 (GSLV Mk III) — India's heaviest launcher, human-rated for Gaganyaan

◦ SSLV — for small satellites on demand

 

• India's launches take place from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh. A second spaceport is being developed at Kulasekarapattinam in Tamil Nadu for small-lift launches.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 are incorrect because Statement 1 is factually accurate while Statement 2 misstates both the number of stages and the type of propulsion used.

question: Which enzyme unwinds the double helix of DNA during replication?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Helicase.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Helicase is the enzyme that unwinds the DNA double helix during replication, by breaking the hydrogen bonds between the complementary base pairs and separating the two strands to create the replication fork. (हेलिकेज़ — डीएनए की कुंडली खोलने वाला एंजाइम)

 

• The main enzymes of DNA replication and their roles:

◦ Helicase — unwinds and separates the two strands

◦ Topoisomerase (gyrase) — relieves the supercoiling created ahead of the fork

◦ Single-strand binding proteins — keep the separated strands apart

◦ Primase — lays down a short RNA primer to start synthesis

◦ DNA polymerase — adds nucleotides in the 5' to 3' direction and proofreads

◦ DNA ligase — joins the Okazaki fragments on the lagging strand, sealing the nicks

 

• DNA replication is semi-conservative, each new molecule retaining one parent strand — as demonstrated by the Meselson and Stahl experiment of 1958.

 

• The double helix structure of DNA was proposed by James Watson and Francis Crick in 1953, using the X-ray diffraction work of Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• DNA contains the bases adenine, guanine, cytosine and thymine; in RNA, thymine is replaced by uracil. Chargaff's rule states that A pairs with T (two hydrogen bonds) and G with C (three hydrogen bonds).

 

• Telomerase is an enzyme that lengthens the telomeres, the repetitive protective sequences at the ends of chromosomes, and so counters their shortening at each round of cell division.

 

NOTE

 

• DNA ligase (Option 1): Joins the fragments of the lagging strand; it does not unwind the helix.

 

• DNA polymerase (Option 3): Synthesises the new strand by adding nucleotides, but requires the strands to be already separated.

 

• Primase (Option 4): Synthesises the short RNA primer needed by DNA polymerase to begin.

question: The Punchhi Commission, set up by the Government of India in 2007, was constituted to examine which of the following?
option_2: Reorganisation of states on a linguistic basis
solution_text:
The correct answer is Centre-State relations.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Punchhi Commission was constituted in 2007 under the chairmanship of Justice Madan Mohan Punchhi, a former Chief Justice of India, to examine afresh the working of Centre-State relations, in view of the far-reaching changes since the Sarkaria Commission reported in 1988. It submitted its report in 2010. (पुंछी आयोग — केंद्र-राज्य संबंध)

 

• Among its recommendations were: the appointment of a Governor by a committee including the Chief Minister and the Chief Justice of the High Court; a fixed five-year tenure for Governors and their removal only by impeachment-like process; the use of "localised emergency" under Article 355 rather than blanket President's Rule; and consultation with States on Concurrent List legislation.

 

• The earlier Sarkaria Commission, set up in 1983 under Justice R.S. Sarkaria, examined the same subject and made 247 recommendations. It notably recommended making the Inter-State Council operational with a permanent secretariat, and opposed the wholesale dismissal of State governments under Article 356.

 

• The Inter-State Council was finally established in 1990 under Article 263, on the Sarkaria Commission's recommendation, by a Presidential Order.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important committees and commissions:

◦ Rajamannar Committee (1969) — set up by the Tamil Nadu government on Centre-State relations

◦ Administrative Reforms Commissions — the first (1966) under Morarji Desai and later K. Hanumanthaiya, the second (2005) under Veerappa Moily

◦ Venkatachaliah Commission (2000) — the National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution

 

• Centre-State relations in the Constitution are dealt with under three heads: legislative (Articles 245-255), administrative (Articles 256-263) and financial (Articles 268-293).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: Electoral reforms have been examined by bodies such as the Dinesh Goswami Committee (1990) and the Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998).

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: The reorganisation of states was examined by the Dhar Commission (1948), the JVP Committee (1949) and the States Reorganisation Commission (1953) under Fazl Ali.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: The Punchhi Commission's terms of reference concerned federal relations, not the judiciary as such.

question: Why does a pressure cooker cook food faster than an ordinary open vessel?
option_1: The higher pressure inside raises the boiling point of water, so the food cooks at a higher temperature
option_2: The cooker is a better conductor of heat than an ordinary vessel
option_3: The steam trapped inside chemically softens the food
option_4: The reduced pressure inside lowers the boiling point of water
solution_text:
The correct answer is The higher pressure inside raises the boiling point of water, so the food cooks at a higher temperature.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The boiling point of a liquid rises as the pressure on its surface increases. In a sealed pressure cooker, steam cannot escape freely, so the pressure inside rises to roughly twice atmospheric pressure, and the boiling point of water rises from 100°C to about 120°C. (प्रेशर कुकर — दाब बढ़ने से क्वथनांक बढ़ता है)

 

• Food therefore cooks at a higher temperature, and chemical reactions proceed faster, so cooking time is cut sharply and fuel is saved.

 

• The converse follows from the same principle: at high altitudes the atmospheric pressure is low, so water boils below 100°C and food is difficult to cook — which is exactly why a pressure cooker is essential in the hills.

 

• A pressure cooker carries a safety valve and a weight (whistle) on the vent to release excess steam and prevent the pressure from rising to a dangerous level.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Related everyday applications of heat:

◦ Copper or aluminium bottoms are given to cooking utensils because these metals are good conductors of heat, ensuring rapid and even heating

◦ Handles are made of wood or plastic, which are poor conductors (insulators)

◦ Ice is packed in sawdust because sawdust is a poor conductor and traps air

◦ Water has an unusually high specific heat capacity, which is why it is used as a coolant in radiators

 

• Heat travels by conduction (in solids), convection (in fluids) and radiation (which needs no medium).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: A pressure cooker is made of the same metals as ordinary vessels; the gain comes from pressure, not conductivity.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: Steam does not act as a chemical softening agent; the effect is purely thermal.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: The pressure inside a cooker rises; it is at high altitudes that low pressure lowers the boiling point and slows cooking.

question: The Uniform Civil Code for the citizens of India finds mention in which Article of the Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 44.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 44 of the Constitution provides that "the State shall endeavour to secure for the citizens a uniform civil code throughout the territory of India." (अनुच्छेद 44 — समान नागरिक संहिता)

 

• It falls in Part IV, among the Directive Principles of State Policy, and is therefore non-justiciable — it cannot be enforced by any court, though it is fundamental in the governance of the country.

 

• A Uniform Civil Code (UCC) would provide a common set of personal laws for all citizens irrespective of religion, covering marriage, divorce, maintenance, adoption, guardianship, inheritance and succession. It does not relate to criminal law, which is already uniform for all citizens.

 

• Goa has long had a common civil code, inherited from the Portuguese Civil Code of 1867, and Uttarakhand became the first state in independent India to enact a Uniform Civil Code, which came into effect in 2025.

 

• The Supreme Court has repeatedly referred to Article 44, notably in the Shah Bano case (1985) and in Sarla Mudgal v. Union of India (1995).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Some other frequently asked Directive Principles:

◦ Article 39A — equal justice and free legal aid

◦ Article 40 — organisation of village panchayats

◦ Article 41 — right to work, education and public assistance

◦ Article 43 — living wage for workers; Article 43B — promotion of cooperative societies

◦ Article 45 — early childhood care and education for children below six years

◦ Article 47 — raising the level of nutrition and prohibition of intoxicating drinks

◦ Article 48 — organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry, and prohibition of the slaughter of cows and calves

◦ Article 50 — separation of the judiciary from the executive

 

NOTE

 

• Article 43 (Option 1): Directs the State to secure a living wage and decent conditions of work.

 

• Article 45 (Option 3): As amended by the 86th Amendment, provides for early childhood care and education for children below the age of six.

 

• Article 48 (Option 4): Deals with the organisation of agriculture and animal husbandry on modern lines.

question: The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY), launched in 2016, primarily provides which of the following?
option_1: Interest-free loans to farmers for the purchase of tractors
option_2: A guaranteed minimum support price for every crop grown in India
option_3: Crop insurance cover against yield losses caused by natural calamities, pests and diseases
option_4: Free electricity for irrigation pump sets in rural areas
solution_text:
The correct answer is Crop insurance cover against yield losses caused by natural calamities, pests and diseases.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY) was launched in 2016 by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare to provide comprehensive crop insurance against the failure of any of the notified crops as a result of natural calamities, pests and diseases. (प्रधानमंत्री फसल बीमा योजना, 2016)

 

• The premium payable by the farmer is capped at:

◦ 2 per cent of the sum insured for Kharif food and oilseed crops

◦ 1.5 per cent for Rabi food and oilseed crops

◦ 5 per cent for annual commercial and horticultural crops

 

  The balance of the actuarial premium is shared by the Central and State Governments.

 

• The scheme covers prevented sowing, standing crop losses, post-harvest losses for up to 14 days, and localised calamities such as hailstorm, landslide and inundation. Enrolment is voluntary for all farmers since 2020.

 

• Technology is used extensively — remote sensing, drones and smartphone-based crop-cutting experiments through the CCE-Agri app, and the National Crop Insurance Portal for enrolment and claims.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other important agricultural schemes:

◦ PM-KISAN (2019) — income support of Rs. 6,000 a year in three instalments to landholding farmer families

◦ Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (2020) — a Rs. 1 lakh crore financing facility with interest subvention for post-harvest management infrastructure such as cold chains, warehouses and agri-logistics

◦ Soil Health Card Scheme (2015) and the Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana for organic farming

◦ e-NAM (2016) — the online National Agriculture Market linking APMC mandis

◦ Kisan Credit Card (1998) — short-term credit for cultivation needs

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: Farm machinery is financed under the Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanisation and through the Kisan Credit Card, not PMFBY.

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: The Minimum Support Price is announced on the recommendation of the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP) for a specified list of crops, and is a separate mechanism.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: Free or subsidised power for irrigation is a matter of state policy; the related central scheme is PM-KUSUM, for solar pumps.

question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the correct options:

Assertion (A): The PM MITRA scheme aims to develop world-class integrated textile parks in India.

Reason (R): The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Textiles.
option_1: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
option_2: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
option_3: A is true, but R is false
option_4: A is false, but R is true
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Assertion (A) is true. The PM MITRA scheme — Pradhan Mantri Mega Integrated Textile Region and Apparel Parks — announced in 2021, provides for the setting up of seven mega textile parks to create world-class industrial infrastructure for the textile sector. (पीएम मित्र योजना — मेगा एकीकृत वस्त्र क्षेत्र एवं परिधान पार्क)

 

• Reason (R) is true. The scheme is indeed implemented by the Ministry of Textiles.

 

• However, R is not the explanation of A. The identity of the administering ministry is an administrative fact; it does not explain why the scheme aims at building integrated textile parks. That aim arises from the 5F vision — Farm to Fibre to Factory to Fashion to Foreign — under which the entire textile value chain is to be brought to a single location so as to cut logistics costs and attract investment.

 

• The seven PM MITRA park sites are in Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Gujarat, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Maharashtra.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's textile industry is notable for being self-reliant across the full value chain — from fibre and yarn to fabric, dyeing, processing and finished garments — which distinguishes it from most competing countries.

 

• Related schemes: the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Textiles, focused on man-made fibre apparel and technical textiles; the National Technical Textiles Mission; and SAMARTH, for skilling in the textile sector.

 

• India is among the world's largest producers of cotton, jute and silk, and the textile sector is one of the country's largest employers after agriculture.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: Although both statements are true, the implementing ministry does not explain the objective of the scheme.

 

• Options 3 and 4 are incorrect: Both the Assertion and the Reason are factually accurate.

question: The Global Peace Index, which ranks countries according to their level of peacefulness, is produced by which organisation?
option_1: The Stockholm International Peace Research Institute
option_3: The Carnegie Endowment for International Peace
option_4: The Institute for Economics and Peace
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Institute for Economics and Peace.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Global Peace Index (GPI) has been produced annually since 2007 by the Institute for Economics and Peace (IEP), an international think tank founded by the Australian technology entrepreneur Steve Killelea, with headquarters at Sydney. (ग्लोबल पीस इंडेक्स — इंस्टीट्यूट फॉर इकोनॉमिक्स एंड पीस)

 

• The Index ranks independent states and territories using 23 indicators grouped into three domains:

◦ Ongoing domestic and international conflict

◦ Societal safety and security

◦ Militarisation

 

• Since the base year 2008, global peacefulness has on the whole deteriorated: the domains of ongoing conflict and safety and security have worsened, while militarisation has, on average, improved slightly.

 

• Iceland has been ranked the most peaceful country in the world in every edition since 2008.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The IEP also publishes the Global Terrorism Index, the Positive Peace Report and the Ecological Threat Report.

 

• Other indices and their publishing bodies:

◦ SIPRI Yearbook on armaments and military expenditure — Stockholm International Peace Research Institute

◦ Human Development Index — UNDP

◦ Global Innovation Index — WIPO

◦ Corruption Perceptions Index — Transparency International

◦ World Press Freedom Index — Reporters Without Borders

◦ Global Hunger Index — Concern Worldwide and Welthungerhilfe

 

NOTE

 

• SIPRI (Option 1): Founded in 1966 at Stockholm, it studies armed conflict, arms transfers and military spending, but does not publish the GPI.

 

• The UNDP (Option 2): Publishes the Human Development Report and the Multidimensional Poverty Index.

 

• The Carnegie Endowment for International Peace (Option 3): A foreign-policy think tank based in Washington, D.C., which does not produce this index.

question: Which institution has been designated the National Implementing Entity for the National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change (NAFCC) in India?
option_3: The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
option_4: The Small Industries Development Bank of India
solution_text:
The correct answer is The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• NABARD — the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development — is the National Implementing Entity (NIE) for the National Adaptation Fund for Climate Change (NAFCC). (नाबार्ड — एनएएफसीसी की राष्ट्रीय कार्यान्वयन संस्था)

 

• The NAFCC was established in 2015 under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change to meet the cost of adaptation to climate change in those States and Union Territories that are particularly vulnerable to its adverse effects.

 

• NABARD was chosen because it was already the accredited NIE for the Adaptation Fund under the Kyoto Protocol and has a nationwide presence. Its role covers project formulation, appraisal, sanction, disbursement, monitoring and evaluation, and capacity building of State governments.

 

• Projects under NAFCC are drawn from the priorities identified in the State Action Plans on Climate Change (SAPCC), and are concentrated in the most climate-sensitive sectors — above all agriculture and water resources, followed by forestry, coastal zones and disaster management.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• NABARD was set up in 1982 on the recommendation of the Shivaraman Committee, and is headquartered at Mumbai. It is the apex development bank for agriculture and rural development, and refinances regional rural banks and cooperative banks.

 

• The distinction to remember: adaptation means adjusting to the effects of climate change, such as drought-resistant crops, water conservation and coastal protection, whereas mitigation means reducing or preventing emissions at source.

 

• Other climate finance mechanisms in India include the National Clean Energy Fund and, internationally, the Green Climate Fund and the Loss and Damage Fund.

 

NOTE

 

• NITI Aayog (Option 1): The Government's policy think tank, which replaced the Planning Commission in 2015; it does not implement NAFCC projects.

 

• The Central Water Commission (Option 2): A technical body under the Ministry of Jal Shakti dealing with water resources development.

 

• SIDBI (Option 4): The apex financial institution for the micro, small and medium enterprise sector, set up in 1990.

question: Which of the following correctly describes the term 'sunrise industry'?
option_1: An industry that is in decline and is gradually being phased out
option_2: An industry that can be located only in coastal regions
option_3: An industry that is wholly owned and operated by the Central Government
option_4: An industry that is new and fast growing, with strong potential for future expansion, such as electronics and biotechnology
solution_text:
The correct answer is An industry that is new and fast growing, with strong potential for future expansion, such as electronics and biotechnology.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A sunrise industry is one that is new, rapidly growing and has strong prospects for the future, usually driven by new technology and rising demand. (उदयीमान उद्योग — नवीन एवं तीव्र गति से बढ़ता उद्योग)

 

• Examples in the Indian context include information technology and IT-enabled services, electronics and semiconductors, biotechnology, renewable energy, electric vehicles, telecommunications, space technology, drones and artificial intelligence.

 

• The opposite is a sunset industry — an old, declining industry that is losing its market and gradually being phased out, often because of technological change or foreign competition.

 

• The industries in a sunrise sector are generally knowledge-intensive, attract large investment, and enjoy targeted government support such as the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes, which cover sectors including electronics, semiconductors, pharmaceuticals, automobiles and textiles.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other terms used in classifying economic activity:

◦ Primary sector — agriculture, fishing, forestry, mining

◦ Secondary sector — manufacturing and construction

◦ Tertiary sector — services such as trade, transport, banking, education and health

◦ Quaternary sector — knowledge-based activities such as research, IT and consultancy

◦ Quinary sector — the highest level of decision-making

 

• The services sector contributes the largest share of India's Gross Value Added, followed by industry and then agriculture — although agriculture still supports the largest share of the workforce.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: A declining industry that is being phased out is a sunset industry.

 

• Option 2 is incorrect: Location near the coast defines a port-based or footloose-versus-bulk-material classification, not a sunrise industry.

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: Government ownership defines a public sector industry, which is a classification by ownership, not by growth prospects.

question: Which Article of the Constitution empowers Parliament to provide for the adjudication of disputes relating to the waters of inter-State rivers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 262.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 262 empowers Parliament to provide by law for the adjudication of any dispute or complaint relating to the use, distribution or control of the waters of any inter-State river or river valley. (अनुच्छेद 262 — अंतरराज्यीय नदी जल विवाद)

 

• Crucially, Article 262(2) further permits Parliament to provide that neither the Supreme Court nor any other court shall exercise jurisdiction over such a dispute. Parliament has exercised this power.

 

• Under this Article, Parliament enacted two laws in 1956:

◦ the River Boards Act, 1956, for the regulation and development of inter-State rivers

◦ the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956, under which the Central Government constitutes an ad hoc tribunal on receiving a request from a State

 

• Well-known tribunals set up under the Act include those for the Krishna, Godavari, Narmada, Cauvery, Ravi-Beas, Mahadayi and Vansadhara rivers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The neighbouring Articles on inter-State relations (Part XI, Articles 262-263, and Part XIII) are commonly confused:

◦ Article 261 — full faith and credit to be given to public acts, records and judicial proceedings of the Union and of every State

◦ Article 262 — adjudication of inter-State water disputes

◦ Article 263 — provision for the Inter-State Council, which the President may establish to inquire into and advise upon disputes between States and to investigate subjects of common interest

◦ Article 264 onwards — finance, defining "Finance Commission" and related provisions

 

• Water is a State List subject (Entry 17), while the regulation and development of inter-State rivers declared by Parliament to be in the public interest is a Union List subject (Entry 56).

 

NOTE

 

• Article 261 (Option 1): Concerns full faith and credit to public acts and records, not water disputes.

 

• Article 263 (Option 3): Provides for the Inter-State Council, which was set up in 1990 on the recommendation of the Sarkaria Commission; it is an advisory body, not an adjudicatory one.

 

• Article 264 (Option 4): Falls in the chapter on finance and does not deal with river waters.

question:
Evaluate these statements regarding the layers of the atmosphere:

1. The troposphere is the lowest layer of the atmosphere and contains almost all the water vapour and dust.

2. Temperature increases with height within the stratosphere, because ozone there absorbs ultraviolet radiation.

Which of the above is/are correct?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 2.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statement 1 is correct. The troposphere is the lowest layer of the atmosphere, extending to about 8 km at the poles and 18 km at the equator. It holds nearly all the water vapour, dust and clouds, and is therefore the layer in which almost all weather phenomena occur. Temperature falls with height here, at the normal lapse rate of about 6.5°C per 1,000 metres. (क्षोभमंडल — सभी मौसमी घटनाएँ)

 

• Statement 2 is correct. In the stratosphere, extending from the tropopause to about 50 km, temperature increases with height. The reason is the ozone layer, at roughly 15 to 35 km, which absorbs the sun's harmful ultraviolet radiation and warms the surrounding air. The stratosphere is free of cloud and turbulence, which is why jet aircraft fly in its lower part.

 

• The layers of the atmosphere in order are: Troposphere - Stratosphere - Mesosphere - Thermosphere (Ionosphere) - Exosphere, separated by the tropopause, stratopause and mesopause.

 

• The mesosphere is the coldest layer, where meteors burn up; the thermosphere or ionosphere reflects radio waves back to earth and is where the aurora occurs; and the exosphere is the outermost, merging into space.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• By volume, dry air is about 78 per cent nitrogen and 21 per cent oxygen, with argon, carbon dioxide and trace gases making up the rest.

 

• Ozone (O₃) is depleted by chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs). The Vienna Convention (1985) and the Montreal Protocol (1987) provide for phasing out ozone-depleting substances, and 16 September is observed as the International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are incorrect because both of the given statements are factually accurate. Candidates are often misled by the reversed version of these statements — that weather occurs in the stratosphere and that ozone lies in the troposphere — which is wrong on both counts.
